correctness.rationale: The Heawood edge endpoints have distinct closed neighborhoods. With at most three colors, both endpoint signatures contain the two endpoint colors, so they must have sizes two and three, alternately by shore. The neighbors of each size-two vertex all have one color; connectivity forces the entire size-three shore monochromatic, and its corresponding incident Fano triples on the other shore must be bichromatic. Every pair lies in a unique triple (also in the dual), so bichromatic triples would give seven monochromatic pairs, whereas the two class sizes give at least nine. The fresh finite enumeration yields a nonempty four-color state set, establishing optimality. It exhausts all point assignments and proper line extensions and checks every incidence, then tests all one-vertex and exactly-two-vertex replacements with both changed colors distinct from their old values. It reproduces all six profiles, 54,264 valid states, 185,808 single-change edges, exactly 6,048 frozen states of profile (3,3,2), all eight shore-and-color components of size 882, and all six point-core components of size 6,860 with the stated per-component counts. Exactly-two changes give 897,456 edges and one component, which suffices also for budget two. The first frozen C++ verifier joins one- and two-changes for its connectivity check and alone proves only at-most-two connectivity; the second frozen verifier uses genuinely exact-two joins, and the fresh replay separately verifies this stronger claim.
residual_risks: The finite check is for the labeled Fano incidence graph with four named colors and exact simultaneous moves, not a claim about isomorphism types of equal-order components or a proof-assistant certification.

evidence: Heawood is the Fano incidence graph, with no edge having equal closed endpoint neighborhoods. LID compares the sets of colors of these closed neighborhoods on every edge. Ordinary proper colorings do not check those sets, and two-homogeneous colorings instead constrain the number of colors in each open neighborhood.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Neither named-color conventions nor relabeling the graph can turn these different predicates into the submitted predicate, as the distinct state counts and exact disjointness check show.

originality.rationale: The optimal palette size and the basic locally identifying predicate are prior. Neither the general large-palette recoloring lemma nor the closest same-graph, same-palette recoloring census supplies the actual state graph at the four-color LID optimum. The strongest same-day candidate uses an open-neighborhood condition whose accepted set is disjoint from the present one in a complete replay, despite the coincidental common number 6,048. The exact support-based component classification and exact-two threshold are the supported distinct claims.
residual_risks: Originality is bounded by inspected comparisons; unindexed equivalent classes or exact tables could remain. No novelty claimed for the LID chromatic number four.

value.rationale: The Fano incidence graph is a natural smallest projective-plane case, and the palette is fixed by the known optimum, not an arbitrary cutoff. A large frozen sector, explicit shore/core labels for all remaining components, and the exact restoration of global mobility by changing two vertices give a benchmark for optimal locally identifying reconfiguration quite different from the ordinary and open-neighborhood coloring graphs.
residual_risks: The benchmark does not establish a threshold for larger incidence graphs, other palettes, or additional distance or symmetry claims.
